The population $y(t)$ of giraffes on a certain African wildlife reserve follows the logistic growth model

$$
{y}^{′}=14.4y-0.003{y}^{2},\,y(0)=150,
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years, since the observations began. According to this model, what is the maximum possible population of giraffes?

feedback.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
{y}^{′}=ky(a-y),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>y$ is the carrying capacity. 

The carrying capacity $a$ represents the maximum possible population. A diagram showing a typical logistic growth curve is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071800/assets/d8133f1c4203903bac606bbae61c73717e2ba2dc15a97a77f48eaaeaf4736d06.png)

First, let's rewrite the right-hand side of the given equation so that it matches the form above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =14.4y-0.003{y}^{2} \\  & =0.003y(4800-y)\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that $a=4800.$ Hence, the carrying capacity is $4800,$ and we conclude that the maximum possible population of giraffes is $4800.$
